topics.title: Welcome
topics.step:
This plugin tidies the folder tree Penumbra shows you. It never edits, renames or deletes your mod files, and it never changes what a mod does in game.

This walkthrough has eight short steps. As you go, the plugin window behind this one switches tab and outlines what to press. You can leave at any time - it will not come back.

topics.title: Step 1: Scan
topics.step:
Open the Scan tab and press Refresh mod list (outlined in the plugin window).

That reads your library from Penumbra and works out what kind of mod each one is. Nothing else in the plugin updates on its own, so this comes first, and again whenever you install or remove mods.

topics.title: Step 2: Protect anything that must not move
topics.step:
On the Protect tab, tick any mod or folder that should keep exactly where it is. Protected items are skipped by every sort and by Apply. Protect all protects everything.

Mods from Heliosphere and Proteus are left alone by default. If you use them, a dropdown per tool lets you sort them inside their own folder or treat them like any other mod.

topics.title: Step 3: Choose a layout
topics.step:
On the Sort tab, keep the Recommended layout or switch to Advanced to change any kind of mod, and press Sort.

Nothing moves yet. Sort only works out where each mod would go. Your choices are remembered for next time.

topics.title: Step 4: Check the plan
topics.step:
The Review Changes tab shows every mod's current folder beside the proposed one.

Anything that would block the move is listed at the top in red. Two mods landing on the same path is the usual one, and Protect & Skip All Blocking Mods clears them in one go. You can also export the plan to a workbook, edit it in Excel and import it back.

topics.title: Step 5: Apply
topics.step:
When the plan looks right, press Apply (outlined). That is the only step in this loop that changes your library.

A backup is taken automatically first. If some mods could not be moved, a Show failed mods button names them and says why.

topics.title: Step 6: Undo
topics.step:
The History tab keeps a backup from before every Apply. Press Restore on one to put your library back exactly as it was.

Protection does not block this, so it works even for mods you protected afterwards.

topics.title: That is the whole loop
topics.step:
Scan, protect, sort, review, apply.

Every control has an explanation if you hover it, and the Help tab holds all of them at greater length along with a link to the full guide. You can reopen this walkthrough from there.

topics.title: Penumbra is not responding
topics.step:
This plugin reads everything through Penumbra, and Penumbra does not appear to be loaded right now.

Enable Penumbra, then reopen this window and the walkthrough will start properly. Nothing here will work until then, so there is no point walking you through it now.

topics.title: What this plugin does
topics.body:
It proposes a tidy folder layout for your Penumbra mod list, shows you the whole plan, and only changes anything when you press Apply.

It organises the folder tree Penumbra shows you. It never edits, renames, moves or deletes the mod files themselves on disk, and it never changes what a mod does in game.

The usual order is: Scan to read your library, Protect anything that must not move, Sort to propose a layout, Review Changes to check it, then Apply.

topics.title: What is safe, and what is not
topics.body:
Everything that can change your library is on this list: Apply, Restore, Clean Up Selected Folders, Rollback Folder Cleanup, and the recovery panel's Continue and Restore Previous State. Everything else - scanning, sorting, searching, exporting - is read-only, no matter how it looks.

Sorting never moves anything. It fills in a proposed path for each mod, which you can look over on Review Changes and discard by simply sorting differently.

A backup snapshot is taken automatically before every Apply and every Restore, so there is always a way back. The History tab lists them.

Protected mods are excluded from every sort and from Apply. Restore is the one exception, and it says so: it reproduces a snapshot exactly, including for mods that are currently protected.

topics.title: Scan
topics.body:
Unused mods, a collapsed section at the bottom, lists mods that no collection enables, with their size on disk, and can stage them for a move to an Unused folder.

Reads every mod from Penumbra and works out what kind of mod each one is. Nothing else in the plugin updates on its own, so run this first, and again whenever you install, remove or move mods outside the plugin.

The scan runs in the background and the game stays responsive. If your mod list changes while it is running, the results are discarded rather than shown, because they no longer describe your library.

topics.title: Protect
topics.body:
Marks mods that must keep their current folder. A protected mod is skipped by every sort and by Apply.

Protection comes from three places: the mod's own checkbox, any protected folder above it, and Heliosphere. The note beside a mod says which one applies. Only the first is a per-mod choice you make here.

topics.title: Sort
topics.body:
Proposes a folder layout for your mods. The bar at the top stays in view while the rest scrolls: switch between Recommended and Advanced, press Sort, and see how many mods the sort covers.

Recommended is one tidy layout for every kind of mod. Choose what to sort and how to group, and the example paths show where mods will go. Customise per category opens Advanced.

Advanced lists the 16 kinds of mod. Pick one to set its folder (nest with /, as Equipment/Gear), where its creator folder goes, and which splits it uses. Custom marks a category that differs from Recommended, and Reset to Recommended puts it back. The race, body priority and hair settings sit under the categories they affect.

Rules (in Advanced) file particular mods yourself and win over everything above. They still apply when you sort from Recommended, which says how many are active. Auto sort says what happens when new mods are installed.

Nothing moves. Sort only fills in proposed paths, which you then check on Review Changes before Apply.

The bottom of the tab is manual assignment, for putting specific mods somewhere by hand. The ? beside the Sort button brings you back here.

topics.title: Review Changes
topics.body:
Shows every mod's current folder beside its proposed one, along with anything that would block Apply.

Errors are listed at the top and must be cleared before Apply is available. A collision means two mods would end up at the same path; a protected-mod error means something tried to move a mod you protected.

This tab also holds folder cleanup, which removes empty folder entries left behind in Penumbra's own folder file. That is separate from moving mods and has its own backup.

topics.title: History
topics.body:
Every backup snapshot, newest first. A snapshot records where each mod was at that moment.

Backups are taken automatically before each Apply and Restore, and you can take one yourself at any time with an optional label.

Restore is exact: it reproduces the snapshot's paths even for mods that are currently protected or Heliosphere-managed. That is deliberate, and it is the one place protection does not apply.

topics.title: Search
topics.body:
Looks up which mod changes a given item. Entirely read-only.

Build the index first, then filter by mod name, by item name, by category, and by equipment slot for gear.

Since Penumbra 1.7 its own Mods tab has a native search syntax that covers much of this, so this tab may be retired later.

topics.title: If something went wrong
topics.body:
If an Apply or Restore is interrupted - a crash, a force-quit, the game closing mid-operation - the plugin notices on the next start and shows a recovery panel above the tabs. Nothing else can run until you resolve it.

You get three choices: accept the current state and move on, finish what was interrupted, or roll back to how things were before it started. The panel says which are available; a greyed-out option means the plugin no longer has the file it would need.

If several operations were interrupted, they are resolved one at a time, and the per-operation buttons permanently abandon that one operation rather than repairing it.

For anything else, Create Diagnostic Dump on Review Changes writes a file describing the plugin's state, which is the most useful thing to attach to a bug report.

topics.title: Where your files are
topics.body:
This plugin keeps its own settings, backups and exports in its Dalamud config folder. Show Config File on Review Changes opens it.

The folder tree you see in Penumbra lives in Penumbra's own organization.json, not here. Folder cleanup is the only feature that writes to it, and it takes a backup first.

Your actual mod files are never touched by this plugin, wherever Penumbra keeps them.

topics.title: Refresh mod list
topics.short: Re-reads every mod from Penumbra and re-classifies it. Nothing moves. Run it after installing, removing or moving mods elsewhere - nothing here updates on its own.

topics.title: Live events
topics.short: Penumbra events as they happen. Informational only: seeing a mod appear here does not re-scan, so run Refresh mod list yourself afterwards.

topics.title: Protect all / Unprotect all
topics.short: Protects every mod if any are unprotected; when all are protected, the button reads Unprotect all and clears them. A protected mod keeps its current folder through every Sort and Apply.

topics.title: Heliosphere mods
topics.short: Protected: never moved. Sort inside their folder: moved only beneath the folder they sit in. Treat as normal: sorted like any other mod. Saved between sessions.

topics.title: Sort inside folders
topics.short: Keeps a folder (or a sub-folder, like "Characters/Alice") as the top level and sorts its mods beneath it. Everything inside is re-sorted; protected mods stay put.

topics.title: Proteus mods
topics.short: Mods Proteus made. Protected: never moved. Sort inside their folder: moved only beneath the folder they sit in. Treat as normal: sorted like any other mod. Saved between sessions.

topics.title: Proteus managed mod at the root
topics.short: Proteus's own working mod. Kept protected by default. Tick this to place it at the top level of Penumbra's mod list on the next sort; moving it does not affect Proteus.

topics.title: Proteus mod
topics.short: Made by Proteus. It is protected because Proteus mods are set to Protected; change that in the Proteus mods dropdown above.

topics.title: Protected folders
topics.short: Protects every mod in a folder and its subfolders. Click a box to cycle protect, exclude, inherit, so one subfolder can stay free inside a protected one. Folders form a tree: click the arrow to open.

topics.title: Unprotect everything inside a folder
topics.short: Clears protection from every mod in this folder - the mod's own tick, Protect all, this folder or Heliosphere alike. Use it to sort one folder and leave the rest protected.

topics.title: Protect, exclude, or inherit
topics.short: Click a box to cycle protect, exclude, inherit. Dim = inherited from a parent; solid = set here. Exclude frees mods under a protected parent, except hand-ticked and Heliosphere mods.

topics.title: Protected mods
topics.short: Protects one mod wherever it sits. A mod can also be protected by its folder or by Heliosphere - the note beside it says which, and those have no checkbox here.

topics.title: Protected by Heliosphere
topics.short: Protected because Heliosphere manages it, not by its own checkbox. Heliosphere owns where it lives, so the plugin never proposes moving it during Sort or Apply.

topics.title: Group by
topics.short: Sets the folder structure. Creator: Creator/Mod. Mod type: Gear/Mod. Type then creator: Gear/Creator/Mod. Creator then type: Creator/Gear/Mod. A category's own Creator folder wins.

topics.title: Gear: Equipment slot
topics.short: Puts gear mods in Gear/Feet, Gear/Head and so on instead of a single Gear folder. Mods whose slot could not be identified stay in Gear.

topics.title: Gear: Hands and feet in one shared folder
topics.short: Gloves, boots and nails fit most bodies, so they go in Gear/03. Hands and Gear/05. Feet, not under each body. Tops, legs and sets stay under their body. Needs both gear splits, slot and body.

topics.title: NPC: Kind
topics.short: Puts NPC mods in NPC/NPCs, NPC/Bosses or NPC/Enemies. Turn it off to keep every NPC mod in one NPC folder.

topics.title: Recommended or Advanced
topics.short: Recommended is one tidy layout for every kind of mod. Advanced lets you change each category: its folder, creator folder and splits. Both sort the same library.

topics.title: Categories
topics.short: Pick a kind of mod to edit its layout. Custom marks one that differs from Recommended; the rest follow Recommended, including later improvements.

topics.title: Folder
topics.short: The category's top folder. Nest with /, as Equipment/Gear. Relative, no empty part, . or .., at most 260 characters. Nothing moves until you Sort and Apply.

topics.title: Creator folder
topics.short: Where this category's creator folder goes: none, before the type folders or after them. Picking what Group by already gives keeps following Group by.

topics.title: Splits
topics.short: Each split adds a folder level, numbered by depth. The order is fixed. A greyed split keeps its tick and says why it does not apply right now.

topics.title: Example
topics.short: Where a typical mod of this kind would go with these settings, with the creator, folder and splits in their own colours. It updates as you change anything.

topics.title: Select all splits
topics.short: Turns on every split in every category and Split by race, and turns off the shared hands and feet folder. Folders, creator levels and priorities stay. Nothing moves until Apply.

topics.title: Reset to Recommended
topics.short: Puts this category, or with Reset all every category, back on Recommended: folder, creator folder and splits. Nothing moves until you Sort and Apply.

topics.title: How sorting works
topics.short: Opens the Help tab at Sort, which explains how sorting works and what each option does.

topics.title: How a hair mod is filed
topics.body:
A hair mod is filed under one hair number when the plugin can tell which hair it replaces.

If Priority race names a race that has exactly one hair number in the mod, the mod goes under that number, whatever the other races use.

Otherwise, if the whole mod uses one hair number, it goes under that number.

If the mod uses different numbers across races, the Midlander fallback can settle it. It uses the Midlander number when male and female Midlanders agree, or the only Midlander number when one gender is present. Otherwise the mod stays in the plain Hair folder.

A race with two hair numbers in the same mod never picks one, so that mod stays in Hair.

topics.title: Hair: Hair number
topics.short: Files a hair mod under the vanilla hair number it replaces, as Hair/115, padded to three digits (Hair/002) so Penumbra lists them in order. Several numbers or unreadable files: stays in Hair.

topics.title: Hair: Race
topics.short: Files a hair mod under its race, as Hair/Viera/115, while Split by race is on. Several races or none go under Hair/Multi-race.

topics.title: Sort rules
topics.short: Rules file mods with a small SQL-like condition: name contains 'x' -> Folder. The first match wins, unmatched mods sort as usual, protected mods never move. Open this topic for the language.
topics.body:
A rule says: if a mod matches this condition, file it in this folder.

name contains 'hrothgar' and type = 'Body' -> Body/Hrothgar/{creator}

The part before the arrow is the condition. The part after it is the folder; the mod's own name is added at the end.

Rules are edited on the Advanced screen of the Sort tab. They still apply when you sort from Recommended, which shows how many rules are active.

HOW RULES ARE APPLIED
Rules are checked from the top of the list and the first enabled rule that matches files the mod, so the order is the priority (use Up and Down). The rule's folder replaces the whole path the Sort would have chosen, so the mod is not split by body, race or number underneath it. A mod no rule matches sorts as usual. Protected mods are never touched. Untick a rule to turn it off without deleting it. You can have up to 100 rules of up to 300 characters.

SQL-LIKE, BUT NOT SQL
The condition follows the WHERE part of a SQL query, so SQL experience carries over, but you cannot paste a query in. It is deliberately small.

Fields (all text):
name - the mod's name
author - the creator, as the Sort tab names it
folder - the folder the mod is in now (empty in the root)
type - the category folder: Gear, Weapon, Face, Hair, Body, Skin, NPC, Minion, Mount, Pet, Ornament, Furniture, Sound, Animation and VFX, or Review
subtype - the slot or kind inside a category, such as Feet
race - what {race} gives, including Multi-race
body - the body type, such as Bibo+

Operators: =, !=, contains, starts with, ends with, in ('a', 'b'), and not before an operator (name not contains 'x', type not in ('Gear')). Combine with and, or, not and brackets. not binds tightest, then and, then or.

Same as SQL: text goes in single quotes and '' means a quote inside the text (author = 'O''Brien'); keywords and field names are not case sensitive; text comparison ignores case, so 'hrothgar' matches Hrothgar.

Different from SQL: use contains, starts with and ends with instead of LIKE (there are no % or _ wildcards). There is no NULL: a missing author or race is empty text, so write race = '', not IS NULL. There is no <>, BETWEEN, LIKE, numbers, functions or ORDER BY; write != for not equal. contains '', starts with '' and ends with '' are rejected because they would match every mod; = '' and in ('') are fine.

THE FOLDER
The folder can use {type}, {creator} and {race}. A token that comes out empty drops that folder level, so {race}/{creator} on a mod with no race gives just the creator. If the whole folder comes out empty the mod stays where it is and the Sort summary says why. An unknown token is an error.

EXAMPLES
author = 'Ann' -> Ann's mods
type = 'Gear' and subtype in ('Top', 'Legs') -> Gear/Outfits
race = 'Viera' and type = 'Hair' -> Hair/Viera/{creator}
name contains 'recolor' or name contains 'retexture' -> Recolors/{type}
not type in ('Gear', 'Hair') and name starts with 'a' -> A/{type}

WHAT THE RULES LIST TELLS YOU
A rule with a mistake shows a red message with the position, for example: Unknown field 'nmae'. Did you mean 'name'? A good rule shows how many mods it wins for. That count leaves out protected mods and mods an earlier rule already wins, so the numbers add up. An amber warning appears if the folder would no longer match the rule's own folder condition (the next Sort may then file the mod somewhere else), or if the folder is inside a protected folder.

Rules apply to every Sort, including the automatic sort of new mods, but not to a template used as a fallback. In Review, As suggested by Sort includes the rules; editing, reordering or switching a rule greys that export until you Sort again. Rules are saved when you leave the text box.

topics.title: Split by race
topics.short: Master switch for every race split: Hair, Face, Eyes, Skin, tails and racial scaling. Off leaves your folders as they are. It splits by race, not gender.

topics.title: Race splits
topics.short: Face, Eyes, Skin, Tails, ears and horns, and Racial scaling get a race folder while Split by race is on. The Body ones need Part and body type. Scan again after updating.

topics.title: Send multi-race mods to Multi-race
topics.short: On: a mod for several races goes to Multi-race. Off: it goes to the top-ranked race it covers (Race priority). No race found, or an unreadable mod, always goes to Multi-race.

topics.title: Race priority
topics.short: Ranked races, highest first, used only when the Multi-race box is off. An unranked race never wins. Separate from Priority race under Hair, which only picks the hair number.

topics.title: Animation: Emote
topics.short: Emote mods go in Animation and VFX/Emotes/<emote name>. Mods with several emotes go in Multiple, face-only ones in Expressions, and ones with no emote name in Undetermined.

topics.title: Weapon: Job
topics.short: Off by default. On: weapon-only mods leave Gear for Weapon/<job>, such as Weapon/SAM. Several jobs go in Multiclass; no known job stays in Weapon. Scan again after changing it.
topics.body: A mod is a weapon when its files replace a weapon model and no gear or accessory; a weapon with a bracelet or a set stays in Gear. The job comes from the game's item data for the items the mod changes, in your client language. A class files with its job (a Gladiator sword is PLD); an Arcanist book, an item several jobs share, or items that disagree go in Multiclass. A weapon whose items match no job stays directly in Weapon. Turning it off and scanning again puts weapons back in Gear.

topics.title: Gear: Body type
topics.short: Files gear under the body it was made for, as Gear/Bibo+/... With Equipment slot also on: 00. Sets, 01.-09. slots, then numbered bodies from 10, in Body priority order.

topics.title: Body: Part and body type
topics.short: Body mods are body replacers (Rue+, YAB...) and SFW variants filed under Body. This groups them under Body/<body>/. Leave it off if you keep one mod per body.
topics.body: With it on, the Body folder is numbered: 00 Skeleton, 01 Physics, 02 Tails, Ears and Horns, then your bodies from 10 by priority, each with Replacer, SFW and Hands and Feet. A mod that is not clearly a part stays in Replacer.

topics.title: First-choice body
topics.short: Your main body. A mod that supports several bodies is filed under this one when it offers it. The others follow the order in the full list below.

topics.title: Check my collection
topics.short: Reads the mods enabled in your active collection and suggests that body as your first choice. Nothing changes unless you press Make first choice.
topics.body:
It counts only body replacer mods that are enabled in the collection. Gear, and add-ons such as skeletons or physics, are ignored because they say what they fit, not which body you wear.

If your collection uses several bodies, or none, it shows nothing to suggest and says so.

topics.title: Body priority
topics.short: When a mod supports more than one body, it is filed under whichever of them ranks highest here. Mods that name only one body are not affected. Move a body with the arrows; your order is saved.

topics.title: Priority race
topics.short: When a hair mod has one hair number for this race, files it under that number. Pick None to turn this off.

topics.title: Midlander fallback
topics.short: When a mod uses different hair numbers across races, uses the Midlander number if male and female Midlanders agree. Otherwise the mod stays flat.

topics.title: Sort
topics.short: Works out a new folder for every unprotected mod and shows it on the Review Changes tab. Your library is not touched until you apply it.

topics.title: What to sort
topics.short: Whole library sorts every unprotected mod. Only loose mods in the root leaves anything already in a folder alone. This choice is not saved.

topics.title: Sort scope
topics.short: How many mods the last sort covers, out of the whole library, and how many protected root mods were left where they are.

topics.title: New mods popup
topics.short: Shown when mods are installed. Sort now rescans and lists where each new root mod would go, for you to Apply. Review first opens the Review tab. Not now keeps them pending.

topics.title: Don't show this popup
topics.short: Stops this popup. New mods still wait, with one chat line. Turn it back on in Sort > Auto sort.

topics.title: Confirm sort
topics.short: Lists each mod and the folder it would move to. Apply moves them (undo from History). Review first opens the Review tab. Cancel discards this sort and moves nothing.

topics.title: When new mods are installed
topics.short: Ask shows a popup. Sort automatically sorts and applies new root mods without asking (more than 20 at once falls back to the popup). Do nothing ignores them.

topics.title: Show a popup when new mods are found
topics.short: Off: no popup when mods are installed. One chat line replaces it. Has no effect under Do nothing.

topics.title: Unused mods
topics.short: Lists mods that no collection enables, using each collection's own settings, with their size on disk. Reads only; nothing changes.

topics.title: Move selected to Unused
topics.short: Stages the ticked mods under the Unused folder, keeping their folder structure. Nothing moves until you apply on Review Changes.

topics.title: Protect the Unused folder
topics.short: Adds a saved protect rule for the Unused folder so a later whole-library sort does not pull those mods back out. Visible on the Protect tab.

topics.title: Also use the NPC list scraped from the wiki
topics.short: Recognises far more character names, at the cost of matching some very common words. Turned off in this version while we confirm it is safe.

topics.title: Import Workbook
topics.short: Reads your folder choices and any custom categories back from an exported workbook and stages them for review. Codes and {type}, {creator}, {race} in a destination are filled in for you.

topics.title: Assign selected mods
topics.short: Sets the proposed folder for every checked mod. Unlike Sort, this does not renumber name clashes - it reports them as errors on Review Changes instead.

topics.title: Refresh NPC list from wiki
topics.short: Rebuilds the opt-in scraped NPC list from the wiki. The curated list bundled with the plugin is separate and never needs refreshing.

topics.title: Apply
topics.short: Moves every unprotected mod whose proposed folder differs from its current one. This is the only control on this tab that changes your library, and a backup snapshot is taken first, automatically.

topics.title: Export
topics.short: Writes the proposed changes to a text file you can read outside the game. Your library is not touched.

topics.title: Show Config File
topics.short: Opens the folder holding this plugin's own settings and data files. Changes nothing.

topics.title: Create Diagnostic Dump
topics.short: Writes a text file describing the plugin's current state, for troubleshooting or a bug report. Your library is not touched.

topics.title: Export mode
topics.short: As is writes each mod's current folder. As suggested by Sort writes the folders the last Sort staged; it is greyed until you Sort, and again whenever the settings or staged paths change.

topics.title: Diagnostics
topics.short: Troubleshooting tools: export the review as text, open the config file, list the mods the last Apply could not move, or create a diagnostic dump to share.

topics.title: Export Workbook
topics.short: Writes every mod and its destination to a spreadsheet you can edit outside the game. Add your own categories (code 17 and up) on the Category Mapping sheet, then bring it back with Import Workbook.

topics.title: Protect & Skip All Blocking Mods
topics.short: Protects every mod named in the errors above so it stops blocking Apply. Those mods keep their current folder instead of moving.

topics.title: Re-read organization.json
topics.short: Re-reads Penumbra's folder file from disk to refresh the list below. If Penumbra has not written a change out yet, re-reading will not reveal it.

topics.title: Clean Up Selected Folders
topics.short: Removes the checked empty folder entries from Penumbra's folder file. No mod is touched. Run Rediscover Mods in Penumbra afterwards.

topics.title: Rollback Folder Cleanup
topics.short: Restores Penumbra's folder file from the backup taken before the last cleanup, undoing that cleanup only. No mod is moved.

topics.title: Create Backup
topics.short: Saves every mod's current folder as a snapshot you can return to later. Backups are also taken automatically before every Apply and Restore.

topics.title: Restore
topics.short: Moves every mod back to the folder it had in this snapshot. Exact: it moves protected and Heliosphere mods too, which Sort and Apply never do.

topics.title: Delete snapshot
topics.short: Deletes this backup permanently, after you confirm. Your mods are not touched - only the saved snapshot goes, and it cannot be recovered afterwards.

topics.title: Build/Refresh Index
topics.short: Reads every mod's changed items from Penumbra and builds the searchable index below. Read-only: it never moves, protects or alters a mod.

topics.title: Mod name contains
topics.short: Shows only mods whose name contains this text. It combines with the item filter and the category boxes - a mod has to satisfy all of them.

topics.title: Item contains
topics.short: Shows only mods that change an item whose name contains this text, such as one specific piece of gear.

topics.title: Categories
topics.short: Limits results to these mod categories. Unknown covers mods whose changed items the plugin could not classify.

topics.title: Slots
topics.short: Limits Gear results to these equipment slots. Unresolved covers gear whose slot could not be pinned to a single unambiguous match.

topics.title: Keep Current State
topics.short: Accepts whatever Penumbra has now as correct and unblocks the plugin. Nothing is moved or undone - the interrupted operation is simply closed.

topics.title: Continue
topics.short: Finishes the interrupted operation from where it stopped, moving the mods it had not reached yet.

topics.title: Restore Previous State
topics.short: Moves every mod back to where it was before the interrupted operation started, undoing the part of it that did complete.

topics.title: Keep Current State (one operation)
topics.short: Permanently abandons this one operation - it can never be continued or rolled back. The rest stay blocked, and one of them may then become resolvable on its own.

topics.title: Accept Current State and Close All Interrupted Operations
topics.short: Permanently abandons every interrupted operation at once. None can be continued or rolled back. No mod moves - it only stops the plugin blocking further actions.

topics.title: Export my layout as a template
topics.short: Builds a shareable template from the folders your mods are in now, not from pending proposals. A review screen opens first, because a template lists your mod names.

topics.title: Template name
topics.short: How your template appears in someone else's list. Required. The file on disk gets a tidied version of it, but this is the name other people see.

topics.title: Fallback grouping
topics.short: Where an importer's mods go when your template does not mention them. Same groupings and splits as the Sort tab; hair and body use the importer's own settings.

topics.title: Folders
topics.short: Every folder that goes into the template, empty ones included, so an importer gets your whole structure. Unticking a folder also leaves out the mods inside it.

topics.title: Search mods
topics.short: Narrows the list you are looking at. It never changes what is included - Include all and Exclude all always apply to every mod, not just the ones shown.

topics.title: Save to templates folder
topics.short: Writes the template as a .json file you can send to anyone. Use this for a real library: it works at any size, unlike a share code.

topics.title: Copy share code
topics.short: Copies the template as one line of text to paste into chat. Small templates only - a chat message holds about 2000 characters and a big library will not fit.

topics.title: Templates
topics.body:
A template is a folder layout someone shared. Importing one proposes where your mods would go; mods you both have land where they put them, and the rest follow the fallback grouping they chose.

Nothing is applied until you review it on Review Changes.

Export builds a template from your own library. It shows you every mod name that would be included first, because whoever you send it to can read that list.

topics.title: Refresh list
topics.short: Re-reads the templates folder. Use it after dropping a .json in there yourself. Files that are not readable templates are listed as skipped rather than hidden.

topics.title: Open templates folder
topics.short: Opens the folder templates are kept in, creating it if it does not exist yet. Handy for putting a file there by hand, or for finding one you saved to send to someone.

topics.title: Import template file
topics.short: Copies a .json someone shared into your templates folder. It is checked before it is stored, and it never overwrites a template you already have - a name clash gets a numbered filename.

topics.title: Preview against my library
topics.short: Works out where this template would put your mods and shows the folder tree with counts, plus how many of your mods it matched. Nothing is staged or moved yet.

topics.title: Apply this template to my proposals
topics.short: Fills in proposed paths from the preview. Still nothing moves - open Review Changes to check them and apply from there, exactly as with any sort.

topics.title: Protected mods at the top level
topics.short: Protected mods outside any folder. Sorting never moves a protected mod, so these stay at the top level until you untick one. Heliosphere installs new mods here and they are protected on sight.
